query: Based on the conversations, how do members of the group position themselves on using AI-based image enhancement tools like BlurXTerminator?
gold: Felix automates BlurXTerminator as step 4 of his 12-step processing macro. Marcus uses it selectively — yes on stars, no on nebulosity. Aida uses BlurXTerminator on stars but has stopped using NoiseXTerminator after a comparison favored traditional masked stretch. Lena uses BlurXTerminator sparingly, always with a disclaimer, after seeing a published blind comparison. Esme followed Lena's update and adopted the same disclaimer-first practice. Ravi outright refuses and Otis sides with Ravi. Other members are not clearly positioned on this axis from the conversation.
context:
[1] (about=Maya, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:06:00) okay separately, I want to ask something. is BlurXTerminator a cheat?
[2] (about=Lena, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:08:00) Maya, this is a topic I have changed my view on recently. I have been openly critical of the AI tools. After seeing a careful blind comparison published last month showing minimal hallucination on resolved sources, I have started using BlurXTerminator on my own data with a disclaimer in the caption. So: not a cheat, but document its use.
[3] (about=Theo, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:18:00) Maya, hopefully the variety of opinions here shows you that there isn't one answer. The honest answer is: it's a tool, like any other, and the question is whether you label it.
[4] (about=Marcus, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:16:00) I use BlurX selectively. Stars yes; nebulosity no. The risk-reward calculation differs by structure.
[5] (about=Henrik, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:20:00) From a signal-processing standpoint, BlurX is a structured deconvolution prior trained on PSF-aware data. It is not magical. It does what a careful Richardson-Lucy run would do, but faster, with a learned regularizer. The labeling argument is the right one.
[6] (about=Aida, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:24:00) I've stopped using NoiseXTerminator after a careful comparison with traditional masked stretch. The traditional approach gave me cleaner background noise statistics. BlurX I still use for stars.
[7] (about=Bex, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:28:00) team blurx but no noisex 🤝
[8] (about=Otis, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:14:00) ravi I'm with you fellas, no AI for me either. the C8 and dss are enough
[9] (about=Felix, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:22:00) I automate it into my pipeline. step 4 of 12 in my processing macro.
[10] (about=Sven, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T20:32:00) There is a parallel here to belt-modding. The community goes through cycles of resistance, then adoption, then refinement. AI tools are at the adoption phase. The refinement phase is what we should be working toward.
